title: Export bare vectors and map view outputs through mizu_as_arrow()
description:
`mizu_as_arrow()` now accepts an atomic vector as well as a data frame, and exports it as a single Arrow array. Names, `dim` and `dimnames` are dropped, so a matrix exports flat in column-major order.

The output of a `mizu_map()` collected with `.collect = "view"` now exports without copying, as do received raw vectors (as `uint8`).

The copy path now gives the same Arrow data as the zero-copy path: `NaN` in a copied double column stays a value rather than becoming a null, and a copied character column is always a `large_string`.

Also updates the vendored libmizu, which concatenates `large_utf8` columns in `mizu_arrow_col_utf8()`.

title: Re-send unchanged mizu_as_arrow() columns by reference
description:
Columns exported zero-copy by `mizu_as_arrow()` now travel back by reference. When the Arrow data is sent on over a channel, or returned as a pool result, with such a column unchanged, the send references the original shared region and writes only the columns that are new or modified.

Dropping, reordering and renaming columns, and re-batching rows, keep a column unchanged. Slicing, filtering and converting it do not, and those columns are copied as before.

For a 5M-row frame (about 125 MB), an unchanged round trip goes from 8.5 ms to 0.08 ms. A frame with one computed column copies only that column.

This vendors libmizu shikokuchuo/libmizu#14, whose lazy Arrow open lets a string column sent by reference skip its offsets walk.

title: Clarify template checking for cross-language maps
description:
The cross-language section of `?mizu_map` now says that workers check each result against `.template` by the rules of their own language, with a Python `int` for an `integer64` template as the example. The section is also split into three paragraphs.

Documentation only.

title: Attach accepted task handles to a mid-batch submit error
description:
`mizu_submit_batch()` failing mid-batch now attaches the handles of the tasks already submitted to the raised condition as `accepted`. Those tasks run and stay collectible; previously they were cancelled, or left with no handle to collect them.

* This covers a fatal outcome (pool stopped, result slots exhausted) and an error raised while a task is being submitted, such as a `mizu_pool_trace()` hook's error or a failure to encode a task.

* The field is absent when no task was submitted. An interrupt still abandons the batch and cancels the tasks already submitted.

Also updates the vendored libmizu to current main, which adds `mizu_pool_submit_wake()` (used here to wake workers for the kept tasks) and makes a batch submit wake at most one idle worker per task.

title: Use one handler per map runner and close cached mappings at idle
description:
Two follow-ups to the map overhead work, both on R workers.

* `map_runner()` installs one error handler for the whole runner rather than one per batch. This saves about 2 µs per batch, which the batch ramp pays several times per runner: worker-side runner time for a trivial function drops from 50 to 35 µs at 100 elements and from 158 to 138 µs at 1,000. Error classification is unchanged.

* The idle sweep now closes the mappings of a worker's cached map contexts, instead of only dropping the cache references. Previously an idle worker kept finished maps' regions mapped until its next garbage collection (188 MiB per worker after six 64 + 64 MiB maps); it now returns to baseline immediately.

Measurements are recorded in `dev/bench/notes.md`.

title: Close single-morsel map contexts on workers
description:
Single-morsel runner contexts now stay private and close when the runner exits, so completed spec-stream chunks no longer remain mapped on R workers until GC. Cross-language runners resolve their context once; multi-morsel and native-stream caching are unchanged.

Adds regression coverage, NEWS, and benchmark/residency records.

title: Read raw map x directly in worker batches
description: Raw map batches now read `x` directly from the live shared-memory region instead of allocating and copying a slice for every transition. Descriptor-carried inputs, integer64 values, streaming, and prepared swaps keep their existing behavior.

title: Eliminate spec-stream map copies
description:
Raw-x chunks in a spec stream now stage straight from the original vector, template chunks gather directly into the final accumulator, and R-worker generic histories splice at the global output base — removing one temporary allocation and one copy per chunk on each path.

Slice-range verbs now reject fractional bounds, and the two gather verbs share their storage-type and memcpy helpers.

title: Skip cancellation on clean map collects and close one-shot regions
description:
A clean map collect no longer runs the cancellation scan (all runner handles are already consumed by then), and a non-prepared map collected by value now releases its shared memory immediately rather than at the next GC — resident memory across 16 back-to-back 1M-element maps stays flat instead of growing ~280 MB.

Timeout, error, explicit cancellation, worker-death, and prepared-map behavior are unchanged. A late runner opening its region after the unlink fails harmlessly into its already-cancelled task.

title: Fix map cancellation and speed up character results
description:
Fixes `mizu_cancel()` on collected map handles so it no longer disrupts later runs of a prepared map.

Speeds up character-template maps by assembling results in C and validating and flattening native results per worker batch. Invalid native results now fail fast with their element index; spec maps retain submitter-side validation.

Includes regression and cross-language tests, documentation, and benchmark records.

Tests: 6,129 passed, 0 failed, 7 expected skips. rchk reported zero package findings.

title: Drop the gctorture pin round-trip test
description:
The suite's one gctorture test ran a pin/REF round-trip under per-allocation full GCs. On the Windows CI legs the accumulated suite heap makes those full GCs so expensive that the test intermittently stalls for 20+ minutes — twice seen freezing R CMD check (at this exact test), effectively hanging the run.

Deleting it: every assertion it made is covered elsewhere.

- Pin lifetime across GCs: the sibling tests in the same file exercise the same machinery with plain gc() — "crosses twice, collected one at a time", "cycle intact across many rounds", "teardown releases outstanding pins", "consumer-done releases the staged object".
- A received view re-sending as REF: covered more strongly in test-zc.R — the S4 view re-send, the list view re-send with explicit rc_of() refcount assertions, and the REF validation family.
- Protect discipline under GC pressure: covered statically by the rchk CI gate (zero-findings baseline).

No test coverage is lost.

title: Re-vendor libmizu to fix pool shutdown
description: Re-vendors libmizu to fix pool shutdown sometimes waiting an extra 50 ms after all workers had exited cleanly. Also updates the vendored Arrow code and records the fix in NEWS.

title: Faster by-value Arrow sends and libmizu re-vendor
description:
* By-value sends of Arrow tables are faster, including nested tables and sends that cannot use a shared-memory frame region. They are now written straight from the Arrow buffers.

* Re-vendors the libmizu core at shikokuchuo/libmizu#7. Sending Arrow columns with long all-null stretches is faster, as is sending a table made of several batches or sliced batches that contains nulls.

The `mizu_as_arrow()` docs are updated to describe which sends arrive as a frame and which as a data frame.

title: Re-vendor libmizu Arrow open and null handling
description:
Re-vendors the libmizu core at shikokuchuo/libmizu#6.

* Sending an Arrow table with a factor (dictionary) column is faster.

* Sending Arrow columns where many values are missing values is faster, as is sending a table made of several batches or sliced batches that contains missing values.

No API or wire-format changes. The NEWS entry for Arrow sends is reworded to match.

title: Re-vendor libmizu Arrow conversion kernels
description:
Re-vendors libmizu from main for faster Arrow columns with scattered missing values, factor columns, and temporal values.

The full mizu suite passes, including the Python interop tests.

title: Drop the per-message tryCatch from the channel drain
description:
The async channel drain paid two `tryCatch`s per message — one around the receive, one around each handler call — so R overhead, not the transport, was the per-message floor of `mizu_recv_async()`, `mizu_recv_batch_async()` and `mizu_recv_handler()`.

The foreign-payload decline is an interned condition, so the drain can receive it as a value and match it by identity, exactly as the sentinels work. With that, the `tryCatch`s leave the loop: a new `mizu_channel_recv_notify()` verb returns the decline instead of raising it. The drain also splits into separate promise and handler loops, dropping the per-message mode checks, and batch reads are capped at the drain quantum so one large `n` can't stall the event loop.

Benchmark (in-process channel pair, 16k messages, min of 3 reps):

| drain path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| handler, per message | 5.43 µs/msg | 0.73 µs/msg |
| promise singles | 4.09 µs/msg | 1.10 µs/msg |

title: Keep the pool notify arm standing across emptied registries
description:
Stacked on #21.

The pool's async arm used to drop every time the waiter registry emptied, so each `mizu_collect_async()` cycle paid an arm+disarm pair. Now the arm stays standing once raised: settles and timeout detaches never disarm, and only a wake that finds nothing enrolled drops it.

Publishes only signal slots with a live announce, so an idle standing arm sends no extra signals; sequential async collects keep resolving through the fence path (new regression test pins this).

Full suite passes (6009 PASS, 0 fail/warn, cross-language included). Interleaved A/B against the base branch shows no row movement — the removed pair is below the measurement floor of the async rows (details in `dev/bench/notes.md`). rchk clean.

title: Re-vendor libmizu @ 7b42311
description:
Syncs the vendored libmizu core from v0.1.0 to 7b42311 (the same pin pymizu carries). No ABI or wire-format change.

Brings:

- faster sends of Arrow tables with missing values and integer columns
- faster first reads of large zero-copy views on Linux
- repeated sends of a >64 MB payload now reuse one shared-memory region instead of creating one per send
- a correctness fence for the pool task notify announce, and the new `mizu_pool_collect_terminal` verb (no mizu-side use yet — a follow-up will use it)

Full suite passes (6002 PASS, 0 fail/warn), including the cross-language tests against pymizu.

title: Batch collect settled task waiters in the pool drain
description:
Settled task waiters in the async pool drain now collect in one batched `mizu_pool_collect_terminal()` call per scan, instead of one collect per task from R — the per-settle extptr unwrap and registry conflict walk were wasted work, since the scan has already proved every word terminal and enrolled.

Values are preset as `value` on the waiter envs (a `mizu_caught` box on a per-item failure), so `settle_waiter()` resolves or rejects directly and falls back to the per-task settle only for call-site settles. Collective and map waiters settle as before. Bench rows are flat within noise (they sit in the promises machinery), so the win is asymptotic: no more O(registry) walk per settle, no quadratic drain at depth.

Full suite green including the cross-language legs; rchk clean.

title: Add mizu_recv_batch_async()
description:
Adds `mizu_recv_batch_async()`, the promise counterpart of `mizu_recv_batch()`: one promise resolves with a list of up to `n` messages — short when the burst runs out, never waiting to fill — the high-throughput async receive. Single and batch waiters interleave in FIFO call order; terminal states reject with the classed `mizu_closed` / `mizu_peer_gone` errors, and a timeout detaches as in `mizu_recv_async()`.

Stacked on #24.

title: Fix unaligned reads and improve performance at the same time
description: Fixes #13.

title: Drop rlang from Suggests
description: We only used it in one test.

title: Fix Arrow sends erroring after a map collect
description:
Fixes #19.

An Arrow send after collecting a `mizu_map()` result failed with "attempt to apply non-function". The Arrow helpers and the map-collect closure cached the mizu namespace in the same precious-root slot, and the Arrow path used that slot as its initialization flag — a map collect marked the Arrow cache done without storing any of the Arrow helper functions.

The namespace now lives behind a single shared memo (`mizu_r_ns()` in verbs.c), and each caching site guards on its own slot. Includes a regression test that collects on a map handle before the first Arrow send.

title: Align agent skill name and description with posit-dev/skills
description: The mizu skill is now the r-mizu skill, following convention.

description: Closes #16.

title: Add blogpost to pkgdown menu
description: Satisfies a checklist item in #9.

description: Closes #9.

title: Add `mizu_task_handler()`: collect task results without a promise
description:
`mizu_task_handler()` collects the result of a task without allocating a promise. On hot paths it is ~15x faster than one promise per task.

## Motivation

The per-task promise row is the weakest row in the benchmark suite. It runs at ~10–13k tasks/s. The sync pipelined row runs at ~1M tasks/s. Phase 1 moved the pool waiter registry to C, so mizu's own async cost is now a few µs per task. The rest of the cost is the promises package itself: one `promises::promise()` plus one resolve costs ~52 µs per task, and one `later::later()` costs 5 µs.

The channel side already has this answer. `mizu_recv_handler()` delivers 14.3M msg/s with no promise per message. The pool had no equivalent. Now it does.

## What it does

`mizu_task_handler(task, fn)` installs `fn` as the consumer of the result of `task`:

- `fn` runs exactly once. On success it gets the value. On failure it gets the classed condition that `mizu_collect()` raises on a failed task. Detect the failure with `inherits(x, "mizu_error")`.
- The verb needs only the `later` package, not `promises`.
- If the task has already published, `fn` runs at the call site. If not, `fn` runs from the event-loop drain.
- One consumer per result, as before. A task with a handler refuses blocking collects, `as.promise()`, and a second handler. The reverse holds too. The error message names the consumer.

## Results

2000 tasks, 1 worker, medians of 7 runs (standalone; suite row in parentheses):

| consumer | tasks/s | vs promises |
|---|---|---|
| `promises::as.promise()` per task | 12.9k (10.3k) | 1x |
| `mizu_task_handler()` per task | 200k (90.9k) | 15.5x (8.8x) |

The weakest row in the suite moves from ~1/80th of the sync row to ~1/5th. The dated record is in `dev/bench/notes.md` (2026-10-27).

## Implementation

The change is small and reuses the phase-1 machinery. The C registry gets one new mode (`NTFY_TASKH`): a label for refusal messages, a fallthrough to the task verdict, and a new enroll bound. The R side gets a `taskh` waiter kind. It shares the task settle path with `resolve = reject = fn`. The settle collect is the boxed `mizu_pool_collect_settle`, so there is no handler frame per task. The C delta adds no allocations, so the rchk baseline does not change.

## Tests

- Five new tests in `test-promise.R`: value delivery, condition delivery, call-site settle of a finished task, conflicts in both directions, and argument validation.
- One updated test: mode 4 is now a valid registry mode.
- One new report-only benchmark row: "async per-task handlers".
- Full suite: 5400 pass, 0 fail, 7 skips.

title: Integration into the `later` event loop
description:
- Async `mizu_map()`
- Promises methods for mizu tasks and maps
- Efficient map collection

title: Add streaming mizu_map with .stream = TRUE
description:
Closes #5.

Adds `.stream = TRUE` to `mizu_map()` and `mizu_map_prepare()`. A streaming map never writes the whole of `.x` to shared memory. It sends fixed slices of `.x` to the workers as they take work, under a sliding submit/collect window. Shared-memory use stays bounded by the window times the slice size, not by `sizeof(.x)`.

* Results, ordering, `.template`, `.collect`, `.seed` invariance, and the error taxonomy are unchanged.
* The chunk count defaults to `min(length(.x), 32 * live workers)`, and `.chunks` overrides it outright.
* A `mizu_call()` spec as `.f` errors: streaming needs same-language workers.
* pymizu ships the same feature as `stream = TRUE`, with the same semantics.

Checks: the full test suite (3461 tests) and `R CMD check` pass with 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes. Cross-language map tests pass against the matching pymizu build. rchk is clean. Benchmark rows hold their bands, and the validation runs confirm the footprint model: 6.4% of the region path's shared memory for a 16 MB `.x`, against the model's 6.2%.

title: Add a process-wide default pool
description:
Adds four functions: `mizu_default_pool()`, `mizu_set_default_pool()`, `mizu_with_pool()`, and `mizu_local_pool()`.

A package can now read a default pool that the user sets for the whole session. The setter returns the previous default, so callers can save and restore it. The scoping helpers restore the previous default on exit. The default never overrides `mizu_current_pool()` inside a task.

Closes #3.

title: Dot-prefix formals ahead of `...`
description:
Fixes #1.

`mizu_map(p, 1:3, function(i, x) i + x, x = 10)` used to fail: R matched `x` to the `x` formal, so it never reached the function. The same happened with `f`, `p`, `n`, `e`, and any other name that matched, or partially-matched, a formal before `...`.

This PR renames those formals to `.pool`, `.x`, `.f`, `.expr`, `.exprs`, `.name`, and `.source`, following the convention of `mirai_map(.x, .f, ...)`.

What changed:

* `mizu_map()`, `mizu_map_prepare()`, `mizu_map_run()`: `pool`, `x`, `f` -> `.pool`, `.x`, `.f`
* `mizu_submit()`, `mizu_submit_batch()`: `pool`, `expr`, `exprs` -> `.pool`, `.expr`, `.exprs`
* `mizu_call()`: `name`, `source` -> `.name`, `.source`

Also fixes the `timeout` docs on the `mizu_collect_any()` and `mizu_collect_all()` pages, which showed the wrong text.

New tests cover the collision cases.
